historical_claims.anchor: At a spaceport on a harsh moon, people have constructed a wall.
The wall opens Ursula K. Le Guin's The Dispossessed, published in 1974.
In the early 1970s, as she developed The Dispossessed, she researched anarchist political traditions and utopian literature.
In an interview published by Fifth Estate, Le Guin recalled reading the anarchist books she could find in Portland and named Peter Kropotkin and the Goodmans among important influences.
The book won major science-fiction awards, including the Nebula and Hugo for best novel.
Its political and literary project is announced in a subtitle: An Ambiguous Utopia.

description: Follows Shevek between two societies, examining property, institutions, scientific work, freedom, scarcity, and the unfinished practice of utopia. Covers A wall that faces both ways; Reading toward an anarchist novel; Two worlds, two kinds of possession; The freedom of an unfinished revolution.
